nodes.title: What's Zeme
nodes.copy: Zeme serves New York City’s rental market through products for both renters and real estate teams. I joined as the founding designer with no existing design system or research process. I established the visual language, product flows, and reusable system while supporting discovery and client presentations.

nodes.title: Problem
nodes.copy: One platform had to serve two very different audiences. Brokers and property managers needed dense, precise tools; renters needed a clear, trustworthy path through a stressful search. With no design infrastructure in place, I had to define the foundation while shipping both experiences.

nodes.title: Ship, learn, rebuild
nodes.copy: We launched the first redesign in three months using client context and the signals available to us. Shipping exposed where people dropped off and where the flow conflicted with their expectations. I then worked with clients to rethink those journeys and rebuild the flows around observed behavior.

nodes.title: Success
nodes.copy: After the redesign, 54% of customers onboarded without friction and application completion rose 30%. The platform now supports more than $30M in rental estate across New York City.

nodes.title: Problem
nodes.copy: Rental search asks people to repeat the same work across platforms: set filters, compare listings, and check again before good options disappear. But renters think in tradeoffs, not checkboxes. A shorter commute may justify a higher rent; parking may matter more than square footage. Zeme needed to reduce that ongoing effort, not just return another list.

nodes.title: Solution
nodes.copy: We kept the website for renters who prefer traditional browsing and made iMessage the main conversational flow. Renters can describe what they need in plain language, then refine budget, location, and amenities in the same thread. Zeme interprets each request, searches external rental sources, and returns relevant listings. The design work centered on making that exchange clear and useful.

nodes.title: A New Agentic Experience
nodes.copy: Zeme could keep working after the first conversation. With a renter’s preferences in context, the agent could watch new inventory and send relevant updates without another manual search. I designed the experience around a simple loop: describe a need, review matches, refine preferences, and receive new options. The challenge was making memory and proactive behavior feel useful rather than intrusive.

nodes.title: Design Challenge
nodes.copy: Filters and maps show how a traditional search works. An agent makes many decisions behind the scenes, so renters need to know what it understood and why a listing appeared. I designed for clarifying questions, editable preferences, and timely recommendations. The goal was to give the agent room to help while keeping renters informed and in control.

nodes.title: What's Lookbook?
nodes.copy: Lookbook is a design-inspo MCP that searches curated galleries (Mobbin, Godly, Awwwards, and more) and returns ranked picks with screenshots in chat — so you can say “find me a fintech dashboard” and see real UI references without leaving Cursor.

nodes.title: What's the tool?
nodes.copy: Five tools agents call: list galleries, search across them, browse one source, open a page, or review a brief — each returning ranked design refs with screenshots in chat.

action.label: Copy MCP to AI Agent
action.value: Connect Lookbook MCP at https://lookbook-mcp.onrender.com/mcp (remote HTTP — do not clone or self-host). Use it to search design inspo across galleries and always show returned screenshots inline in chat. Tools: list_sources, search_inspo, browse_source, get_inspo_page, review_brief.

nodes.title: A quieter way to focus
nodes.copy: Hush is a small macOS menu bar app for ambient sound. I designed and built a dial for play, pause, and volume, plus a rail that switches between rain, ocean, white noise, and fire. Sound changes crossfade so listening stays continuous. The interface scales from a visual prototype to a compact menu bar panel, and I packaged the app as a macOS DMG.
